column1: # Which flash attention route encodes an op.
# How the rows are used: flash-attn/gen-routes.cmake compiles them in when CMake configures (routes-table.h). The router
# (flash-attn/router.cpp) walks the rows in order and takes the first one whose cells all match. The Intel tiled route may
# decline (no kernel for the head size), and the walk goes on. No row matches = the op is not taken here. No file is read at run time.
# To add a route: write flash-attn/route-<name>.cpp, add its name to the generator and the router, then add its row.
# In every condition column, any = the column does not restrict the row.
# The first row is the header and is required as written: the generator reads the cells by position.
# Columns
#   order: the place in the walk, counting up from 1 with no gap.
#   route: intel-tiled | scalar | matrix | vec. The encoder the row selects.
#   file: the source file of that encoder, for the reader of this table. The code does not read this cell.
#   needs_matrix: the card has simdgroup matrices: yes | no | any.
#   vendor: intel | not-intel | any.
#   width: the card's simd width: 32 | not-32 | any.
#   batch: small (under 20 queries and a head size that is a multiple of 32) | large | any.
#   kv: the K and V types: same | differ | any.
#   fp8: K is f8_e4m3: yes | no | any.
#   head: the head size the route has a kernel for: a number | any.
#   note: why the row exists or what limits it. Free text, no tab. The code does not read this cell.
order

the vec kernel compiles narrower than it assumes on Intel

only the scalar kernels take two formats
